arcs.position_hint: early era-4 stretch, at the first crossroads after the collapsed bridge
arcs.npc: The Custodian of the Moving Shrine
arcs.prompt: She arrives with the portable shrine, the relic inside, and a route mapped three regimes ago. She asks which lord currently owns the concept of safekeeping.

choices.label: Answer: nobody; the relic travels free
Ask to see the route map

arcs.position_hint: era-7 midpoint, outside the constituent assembly hall
arcs.prompt: The Custodian guards a ledger — the state's debts bound as an heirloom — and cites clause chains at the assembly door. She wants the new constitution to name custody as property's senior claim.

arcs.position_hint: late era-10, in the evacuation corridor behind the field office
arcs.npc: The Custodian in the Bunker Stairwell
arcs.prompt: She carries the ledger through the evacuation and visibly ages decades inside one scene. The handoff requires a living witness and there is exactly one available.

choices.label: Seal it until after the armistice

arcs.position_hint: era-12 finale approach, at the launch-weight weighing station
arcs.prompt: Launch mass is priced per gram and the relic has not been weighed in nine eras. She refuses the orbital assignment outright: the relic has weight for a reason.

choices.label: Ground the relic; send a copy
Weigh it and manifest it anyway
Withdraw it from the program entirely

arcs.position_hint: era-14 third act, at the seed vault threshold beside the test plot
arcs.npc: The Custodian at the Vault Thermostat
arcs.prompt: Freezing hums in one key, the test plot in another. She carried things long enough to know which one the future can actually eat, and she wants the lineage to pick a key.

arcs.position_hint: era-16 final chapter, at the shuttle hatch, no return date posted
arcs.prompt: She guarded the pattern-lock since the brand and asks, first time in the Chronicle, who receives it. The honest answer is nobody, or everyone; she nods. She expected both.

choices.label: She refuses; the lineage goes without

arcs.position_hint: era-14 mid-late, at the geoengineering trial pier
arcs.prompt: Claws freshly cleaned, term sheet slid across: sunshade cheap, fast, side effects hyperlinked. Their representative calls it a pleasure, the tone reserved for collateral.

arcs.position_hint: era-14 late, at the balance-sheet window after the audit
arcs.prompt: Entropy deferred at a handling fee; Section 14 defines later, Section 15 defines later again, more strictly. The signing ceremony is brief; the claw-click is not.

arcs.position_hint: era-16 early-middle, at the cryo-bay admissions counter
arcs.prompt: Sleep sixty years, interest accruing throughout, wake-up fees in a font calibrated for patience. They call unconsciousness a grace period.

arcs.position_hint: era-16 late, at the consolidated statement delivery, one clause per season
arcs.prompt: Every Entropy deal since the digital age, compounded, payable in currency you no longer mint. The final page thanks the lineage for its continued liability, warmly.

arcs.position_hint: era-17 opening set piece, terminal court, eleven seats identical
arcs.prompt: Eleven creditor-minds, one ledger starting at a Bronze Age loan. 'We are prepared to be reasonable — we note we have never needed to be before.'

choices.label: Offer equity in the lineage instead

arcs.position_hint: era-17 finale approach, the terminal review projection wall
arcs.prompt: Every choice projected forward, every fork a contingent beneficiary, recited in order with annotations. They reach the present tense and pause — their first ever suspense.

choices.label: Accept the accounting; close books clean

arcs.position_hint: era-6 opening divergence, west-bound anchorage at dawn
arcs.prompt: The envoy compliments your granaries and leaves measuring tapes behind, visible on purpose. Their house sails west tomorrow; somebody must.

arcs.position_hint: era-7 middle, at the imperial ennobment ceremony you opposed
arcs.prompt: The rival accepts a title from the emperor you opposed and his descendants already salute him. He offers friendship at exactly the market price of your principles.

choices.label: Secure your own patent of nobility

arcs.position_hint: era-10 finale, opposite flags at the armistice table
arcs.prompt: Both houses sign the same paper from opposite sides; the scoreboard since the space age's prequel era adds rows nightly. Their border, your grandchildren, one pencil line.

choices.label: Take the moral line, lose the valley

arcs.position_hint: era-12 climax lane, just past the milestone photo op
arcs.prompt: The rival house plants its flag on the same milestone, photograph first. The scoreboard from this era will be cited at the end of everything.

arcs.position_hint: era-14 late, at the circular-economy expo floor
arcs.prompt: Their loops are closed, elliptical, decorative — three claims, one inspection away. They shipped the story; the market pays for stories with delivery dates.

arcs.position_hint: era-16 final beat, mirror ship passing in the router lane
arcs.prompt: Two hulls exchange telemetry like horoscopes, reading each other's damage reports. The scoreboard reaches its final row: two builds, same void, both still moving.
